questions.s: Concerning the enteric and abdominal autonomics (Last's):
o: The enteric nervous system has 50–100 million neurons
As many as the spinal cord. (Last's p. 327)
In the submucous plexus the ganglion cells lie in small groups
They are scattered singly; groups occur in the myenteric plexus. (Last's p. 327)
Vagal fibres reach the gut only as far as the transverse colon
(Last's p. 364)
Vagal fibres supply the gonads and suprarenals
As far as known, they do not; they do enter the kidney. (Last's p. 364)
The right renal hilum lies just below the transpyloric plane
The left just above, 5 cm from the midline. (Last's p. 364)
The lateral femoral cutaneous nerve is a normal posterior relation of the kidney
It is normally too low. (Last's p. 364)
The costodiaphragmatic recess is the most important posterior renal relation
(Last's p. 364)
The kidney moves about 5 cm with full respiration
About 2 cm. (Last's p. 364)

questions.s: Concerning the obturator and accessory obturator nerves (Last's):
o: In the obturator foramen the nerve lies highest, above artery and vein
(Last's p. 395)
The accessory obturator passes under the pubic ramus with the obturator nerve
It passes over it, like the femoral nerve. (Last's p. 395)
Last's says the accessory obturator should be named the accessory femoral
From posterior divisions of L3, 4. (Last's p. 395)
The lumbosacral trunk is separated from the obturator nerve by the superior gluteal artery
By the iliolumbar vessels. (Last's p. 395)

questions.s: Concerning the sacral plexus in the pelvis (Last's):
o: The lateral sacral vessels lie in front of the sacral nerves
Anterior to the parietal fascia. (Last's p. 395)
The pudendal nerve passes between piriformis and coccygeus lateral to the pudendal vessels
It lies medial to them. (Last's p. 396)
The perineal branch of S4 supplies puborectalis
But not the external anal sphincter. (Last's p. 396)
The posterior femoral cutaneous nerve leaves the pelvis in front of the sciatic
It leaves behind it. (Last's p. 396)
About half the hypogastric nerve fibres are preganglionic
They relay in the inferior hypogastric plexus. (Last's p. 397)
Uterine body pain travels with the pelvic splanchnic nerves
With the hypogastric nerves to T10–L1; lower cervix pain with parasympathetics. (Last's p. 397)
The internal sphincter of the bladder is supplied via the superior hypogastric plexus
(Last's p. 397)
Pelvic veins contain valves
There are none. (Last's p. 395)

questions.s: Concerning the lumbar plexus in the abdomen (Last's):
o: Only T12 and L1 supply the anterior abdominal wall
L2–4 form the lumbar plexus for the thigh. (Last's p. 360)
The ilioinguinal nerve has a lateral cutaneous branch
As the collateral branch of the iliohypogastric it has none. (Last's p. 360)
The subcostal nerve lies below the vein and artery behind the lateral arcuate ligament
(Last's p. 360)
The cisterna chyli lies under the left crus
It lies under the right crus, in front of L1–2, between aorta and azygos. (Last's p. 360)
The iliohypogastric nerve pierces external oblique about 2.5 cm above the superficial ring
(Last's p. 361)
The ilioinguinal nerve enters the inguinal canal through the deep ring
It enters from the side after piercing internal oblique. (Last's p. 361)
The lateral femoral cutaneous nerve may arise from the femoral nerve
Both come from posterior divisions. (Last's p. 361)
The lateral femoral cutaneous nerve passes the inguinal ligament 3 cm from the ASIS
About 1 cm from it. (Last's p. 361)

questions.s: Concerning the genitofemoral and obturator nerves (Last's):
o: The genitofemoral nerve emerges from the anterior surface of psoas
(Last's p. 361)
The obturator nerve emerges from the lateral border of psoas
It emerges medially with the lumbosacral trunk. (Last's p. 361)
The femoral branch of the genitofemoral pierces the femoral sheath
It runs in front of the femoral artery. (Last's p. 361)
The femoral nerve passes beneath the inguinal ligament within the femoral sheath
It passes lateral to the sheath. (Last's p. 361)
Accessory ganglia in psoas relay directly back to L1 and L2
So grey rami to L1–2 from the trunk are sparse. (Last's p. 362-3)
The right lumbar sympathetic trunk lies along the right margin of the aorta
It lies behind the IVC; the left lies along the aorta. (Last's p. 362)
Some lumbar veins may pass in front of the sympathetic trunk
A point in lumbar sympathectomy. (Last's p. 362)
The common iliac vessels lie behind the sympathetic trunks
They lie in front at the pelvic brim. (Last's p. 362)
Last's says "presacral nerve" is a misnomer
The superior hypogastric plexus is prelumbar and a plexus. (Last's p. 363)
Hypogastric nerve fibres supply abdominal viscera
They give no abdominal branches; they relay in the inferior hypogastric plexus. (Last's p. 363)
The least splanchnic nerve relays in a renal ganglion behind the renal artery
(Last's p. 363)
The suprarenal medulla receives postganglionic fibres from the coeliac ganglion for secretion
Preganglionic fibres reach it without relay; coeliac postganglionics are vasomotor. (Last's p. 363)
Normal bladder distension sensation ascends in the gracile tract
Bladder pain uses the lateral spinothalamic tract via both autonomic routes. (Last's p. 380)
Sympathetic bladder fibres arise from T10–12
From L1 and 2. (Last's p. 380)
The detrusor motor centre lies in the medial pontine reticular formation
Reticulospinal fibres descend with the lateral corticospinal tract. (Last's p. 381)
Destruction of the sacral segments produces an automatic reflex bladder
It paralyses the detrusor, with overflow incontinence; lesions above S2 give automatic emptying. (Last's p. 381)
The superficial trigonal muscle receives predominantly sympathetic fibres
Unlike the detrusor. (Last's p. 381)
The male internal urethral sphincter is essential for urinary continence
Last's: it prevents seminal reflux and has nothing to do with continence. (Last's p. 381)
In the empty bladder the three trigone orifices are 2.5 cm apart
Up to 5 cm when distended. (Last's p. 380)
The female bladder neck has a circular internal sphincter
Female muscle there is longitudinal; there is no internal sphincter. (Last's p. 381)
On the left the ureter lies under the apex of the sigmoid mesocolon
(Last's p. 381)
The ureter crosses the obturator artery before the obturator nerve
From above down it crosses obturator nerve, superior vesical artery, obturator artery, obturator vein. (Last's p. 381)
Bladder veins do not follow the arteries
They drain to the vesicoprostatic plexus. (Last's p. 380)
The bladder mucosa contains glands
It has none; mucus in urine is urethral. (Last's p. 381)
A pudendal block will not anaesthetize the whole vulva
The front is L1, separated by the dermatome gap from S3. (Last's p. 410)
The deep external sphincter has a bony attachment
Only the middle (superficial) part attaches to coccyx and perineal body. (Last's p. 410)
The lowest part of the external sphincter lies below the internal sphincter
Forming the intersphincteric groove. (Last's p. 410-11)
Anal glands are mucosal crypts like those of the colon
They are submucosal and may penetrate the internal sphincter. (Last's p. 411)
The pelvic splanchnic nerves are sympathetic
They are the sacral parasympathetic outflow; sacral splanchnics are sympathetic. (Last's p. 396)
Some pelvic splanchnic fibres run with the inferior mesenteric artery to the descending colon
(Last's p. 397)
The inferior hypogastric plexus lies medial to the rectum
It lies lateral to it on the pelvic side wall. (Last's p. 397)
Normal bladder distension sensation travels in the pelvic splanchnic nerves
(Last's p. 397)

questions.s: Concerning nerves of the abdominal wall (Last's):
o: The subcostal nerve supplies pyramidalis
And the lower rectus. (Last's p. 360)
The subcostal lateral cutaneous branch supplies skin between iliac crest and greater trochanter
(Last's p. 360)
The ilioinguinal nerve supplies the root of the penis
(Last's p. 361)
The iliohypogastric nerve pierces internal oblique below the anterior superior iliac spine
It pierces it above the spine. (Last's p. 361)
